scenes.headline: Give an agent a real shell, safely
scenes.sub: Kernel limits, hidden credentials, and a proof before any policy change.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Isolde! Give an agent a real shell and it can leak a key or wreck a disk. This runtime moves the boundary below the agent.

scenes.text: Put the boundary in the kernel, below the agent, and keep the credentials where the agent can never reach them.
scenes.say: The idea. Put the boundary in the kernel, and keep the credentials somewhere the agent can never touch them.

left.title: Landlock
items: A denied open makes no handle
left.say: One control bounds the files. Try to open something outside the set, and the kernel hands back no file handle at all.

right.title: seccomp
right.say: The other blocks the dangerous system calls a workload never needs, and refuses to load any new kernel programs.

steps.say: The agent opens a connection. The kernel pauses that system call instead of failing it, and hands it to a listener outside the sandbox.
That listener is the trusted supervisor, on the other side of the boundary. The agent's own connection never touches the network.
The supervisor checks the request against the policy. No matching rule means no connection leaves the sandbox.
If it is allowed, the supervisor adds the credential and dials out itself. The agent never holds the key.
And before that policy can change, a prover checks the edit. A risky new rule waits for a human to approve it.

left.title: The prover models
left.say: The prover models files, network and process identity. Within those, it proves a policy stays inside a boundary.

right.title: Everything else
right.say: A rule it does not model comes back unsupported. You are told to treat that as a failure, not a pass.

scenes.text: The hard part is making the no live where the agent cannot reach it, then saying how far it reaches.

recap: Files and syscalls: the kernel says no
A prover gates every policy change
scenes.say: To recap. The kernel bounds files and system calls, credentials stay with the supervisor, and a prover gates every policy change.
